title: The Siege of Jerusalem Symbolized

questions.question: What did God tell Ezekiel to take, lay before him, and engrave a city on it (that is, Jerusalem)?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:1 (ESV): "And you, son of man, take a brick and lay it before you, and engrave on it a city, even Jerusalem."

questions.question: What was Ezekiel instructed to put around the engraved brick, representing a siege?
options: Siegeworks, a mound, camps, and battering rams all around it
questions.correctAnswer: Siegeworks, a mound, camps, and battering rams all around it
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:2 (ESV): "And put siegeworks against it, and build a siege wall against it, and cast up a mound against it. Set camps also against it, and plant battering rams against it all around."

questions.question: What was Ezekiel to set up as a wall of iron between himself and the city?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:3 (ESV): "And you, take an iron griddle, and place it as an iron wall between you and the city; and set your face toward it and let it be in a state of siege, and press the siege against it. This is a sign for the house of Israel."

questions.question: On which side was Ezekiel told to lie first, bearing the punishment of the house of Israel?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:4 (ESV): "Then lie on your left side, and place the punishment of the house of Israel upon it."

questions.question: How many days was Ezekiel to lie on his left side for the punishment of the house of Israel?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:5 (ESV): "For I assign to you a number of days, 390 days, equal to the number of the years of their punishment. So long shall you bear the punishment of the house of Israel."

questions.question: How many days was Ezekiel to lie on his right side to bear the punishment of the house of Judah?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:6 (ESV): "And when you have completed these, you shall lie down a second time, but on your right side, and bear the punishment of the house of Judah. Forty days I assign you, a day for each year."

questions.question: What does each day Ezekiel lies on his sides represent?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:6 (ESV): "Forty days I assign you, a day for each year."

questions.question: What did God place on Ezekiel so he could not turn from one side to the other till the days of his siege were met?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:8 (ESV): "And behold, I will place cords upon you, so that you cannot turn from one side to the other, till you have completed the days of your siege."

questions.question: What ingredients was Ezekiel told to gather to make bread for himself to eat during the days he lay on his side?
options: Wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and emmer
questions.correctAnswer: Wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and emmer
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:9 (ESV): "And you, take wheat and barley, beans and lentils, millet and emmer, and put them into a single vessel and make your bread of them."

questions.question: How much of this bread was he allowed to eat each day by weight?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:10 (ESV): "And your food that you eat shall be by weight, twenty shekels a day; from day to day you shall eat it."

questions.question: How much water was Ezekiel allowed to drink each day?
options: Whatever he drew from the well
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:11 (ESV): "And water you shall drink by measure, the sixth part of a hin; from day to day you shall drink."

questions.question: Over what type of fire was Ezekiel initially instructed to bake his bread in the sight of the people?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:12 (ESV): "And you shall eat it as a barley cake, baking it in their sight on human dung."

questions.question: What did eating the bread baked over dung symbolize for the people of Israel?
options: They would eat their bread unclean among the nations where God drives them
They would have a bountiful harvest
They would be purified by fire
Their food would taste like ash in their mouths
questions.correctAnswer: They would eat their bread unclean among the nations where God drives them
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:13 (ESV): "And the Lord said, 'Thus shall the people of Israel eat their bread unclean, among the nations where I will drive them.'"

questions.question: When Ezekiel protested that he had never defiled himself with unclean meat, what did God allow him to use instead of human dung for his fire?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:15 (ESV): "Then he said to me, 'See, I assign to you cow's dung instead of human dung, on which you may prepare your bread.'"

questions.question: God said He would break the supply of... in Jerusalem, and they would eat and drink in anxiety and dismay.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:16 (ESV): "Moreover, he said to me, 'Son of man, behold, I will break the supply of bread in Jerusalem. They shall eat bread by weight and with anxiety, and they shall drink water by measure and in dismay.'"

key_verse_text: Moreover, he said to me, "Son of man, behold, I will break the supply of bread in Jerusalem. They shall eat bread by weight and with anxiety, and they shall drink water by measure and in dismay."
